1_startup.description: Reserve the item before beginning work.
1_startup.store: Save reservation_id only; no token or recovery secret exists.

2_activity.description: Touch activity when useful; there is no lease or heartbeat requirement.

3_status_transition.description: Transition item status using the command for the selected backend.
3_status_transition.note: Direct local mode requires the current status_revision through --expected-revision. Served mode uses the authenticated actor and carries its immutable basis; do not pass --expected-revision or an actor override. Neither command gains authority from a reservation.

4_handoff.description: Reassign the advisory reservation to an incoming session when work continues.

5_release.description: Release the reservation when work is complete and no reassignment is needed.

reservation_model.activity: last_activity_at advances implicitly on successful item-scoped mutations attributed to the reservation's session; 'reservation touch' stays available for work done outside sprintctl. There is no heartbeat and nothing lapses.
reservation_model.conflict_policy: Overlapping reservations are recorded and reported, never refused. Two active execution reservations on one item are a warning to coordinate, not an error, and interrupting another session is a separate explicit act: reservation reserve --interrupt-existing.

session_resumption.description: If context is lost, list reservations and reassign or reserve as appropriate.

shutdown_checklist: For each active reservation: reassign to the next session OR release.
Run 'sprintctl handoff' to write a bundle for the incoming session.

takeup_model.description: Sprint-level takeup is an append-only visibility signal, not ownership proof. Use it to mark which actors are actively looking at or operating on a sprint.
takeup_model.proof_note: Takeup and reservations are advisory coordination signals; neither authorizes mutation.
